q: What do the numbers look like for gas turbine cogeneration in a ceramic plant?
title: Ceramic gas engine cogeneration: numbers
short: BEE's Morbi report sizes two gas engines, 2.72 MW, for a vitrified tile plant: 4.08 million scm of gas a year makes 16.7 GWh, and engine heat replaces 1.64 million scm in the spray dryer. Net CO2 falls about 6,260 t a year. Cost Rs 899 lakh, payback 2.75 years (2010).
audience: Owners of gas-fired vitrified tile plants in Morbi weighing captive power with spray dryer heat recovery

sections.h: How the plant is set up
ul: Two engines of about 1.36 MW each carry the whole plant load of 2,109 kW, 24 hours a day for 330 days.
Of the gas heat, about 40% becomes power, 30% leaves as exhaust that goes straight into the spray dryer, and 20% goes to jacket cooling water, a tenth of which is used to preheat air.
The engines burn 515 scm an hour. Exhaust replaces 155 scm an hour of dryer gas and jacket heat another 52.
The spray dryer needs flue gas at about 550 C and is a plant's largest heat user, so it can take the exhaust without extra fuel.
Grid power avoided: 16,695,360 kWh at Rs 4.15 = Rs 692.85 lakh.
Dryer gas saved: 1,639,440 scm at Rs 15 = Rs 246 lakh.
Engine gas bought: 4,080,914 scm at Rs 15 = Rs 612.13 lakh.
Net: Rs 326.64 lakh a year on Rs 899.11 lakh, so 2.75 years.
Cost includes Rs 494 lakh engines, Rs 105.22 lakh import duty, Rs 80 lakh heat recovery ducting and Rs 50 lakh civil work. Ten days of dryer downtime.

p: The report's summary table shows Rs 1,904 lakh, 11.88 million scm, 23.06 GWh, 9.02 million scm saved and a 3.6 year payback. Its own workings do not produce any of those numbers; the figures above follow the workings. It also says turbine in places, but the equipment priced is gas engines.

sections.h: What changes in your carbon figures
ul: Scope 2 from the grid falls to almost nothing; Scope 1 from gas rises by about 8,370 t.
Each kWh from the engines carries about 0.50 kg CO2, or about 0.30 kg once the dryer gas it replaces is credited, against 0.675 kg from the grid.
Gas engines also release a little unburnt methane, which a full inventory should include.
The case rests on the gas to power price ratio; redo it with today's gas and tariff before you order anything.

example.title: One plant, one year
lines: Dryer gas saved: 1,639,440 scm x 2.05 = 3,361 t
Engine gas burnt: 4,080,914 scm x 2.05 = 8,366 t
The report says 7,405 t, using older grid factors
example.note: Natural gas at our factor of 2.05 kg CO2 a scm and grid at CEA's FY 2025-26 factor, both estimates.

senseible: Senseible reads gas bills and electricity bills into monthly records with CO2, so the move from Scope 2 to Scope 1 after cogeneration shows month by month. The green loan check shows what a lender asks for on a project this size.
